summary: Hardening Gate step 3 — FAILURE-MODE + ADMIN-CONSOLE sign-off. BACKEND: required suites (test_failure_modes.py + test_admin.py + test_device_auth.py) 38/39 PASS. Single failure = TestTokenLifecycle::test_email_confirm_link_is_single_use_and_expires (Resend 429 rate-limit → 502 from ingress; confirmed 'email send failed: 429' in /var/log/supervisor/backend.err.log — environmental, not a product bug). Full suite (minus test_benchmark.py): 167 passed / 7 failed — 6 failures in test_family.py all environmental (Resend 429); test_family_weekly_push.py::test_window_and_week_key fails with pytest-xdist 'Event loop is closed' — pre-existing test-infra issue, not touched here. FRONTEND E2E (web preview 390x844, testIDs). (1) Fresh onboarding backend UP → Home reached, NO service-banner, deviceId(hex 32) + token(len 43) stored in localStorage 'apollo.device.identity.v2'. (2) Backend stopped, cache-cleared re-run: link check https://www.abc.net.au → check-result-state 'Apollo is patrolling', check-result-intel-unavailable pill 'Online check unavailable — on-device checks only' shown, Why row states 'Reputation intelligence was unavailable, so this result is based on on-device checks only.', confidence: low; Why does NOT contain 'No listing found'. Local-known-bad http://192.168.1.10/paypal-login-verify offline still shows 'Apollo is barking' with the intel-unavailable pill (local heuristics survive outage). (3) Home service-banner-title = 'Apollo's security service is having trouble' (502 = 5xx path); service-banner-line = 'Local protection continues where available. New online checks may be unavailable.'; hero remains 'Apollo is barking'/'patrolling' — never 'off duty' or 'unprotected'. (4) Guard mixed-state copy (with protection toggled ON in Guard): guard-master-title = 'Apollo is guarding what he can', guard-master-line = 'Site Guard simulated · Online checks unavailable right now · On-device link checks remain active.' PASS. Note: with protection toggled OFF (mock adapter default requested=false), Guard correctly reads 'Apollo is off duty' from the security layer's requested-flag — this is the truthful reporting the protectionTruth contract mandates and NOT related to backend health. (5) /family reachable during outage; service-banner present. (6) Backend started → /api/health 200 within ~2s; banner-retry tap clears service-banner; Guard line no longer says 'Online checks unavailable'; online link check returns without an intel-unavailable pill. (7) 403 does NOT reset identity: with own bearer, fetch /api/patrol/events?device_id=<other-hex-32> → 403 'That device_id does not belong to this device.'; reload Home → NO identity-reset-card; same deviceId still in localStorage. (8) 401 → explicit reset: admin POST /api/admin/devices/<id>/revoke (204) → subsequent Home/Family fetches 401 → identity-reset-card + identity-reset-why appear; page.reload() → card persists, localStorage identity=null, no silent POST /api/devices/register; tap identity-reset-register → new deviceId (differs from original) written to localStorage, card gone. (9) BOOT-DURING-OUTAGE: cleared localStorage + backend stopped → onboarding finishes and Home renders in 2.5s (< 20s), service-banner + home-mock-pill visible, local Check-a-link still barks correctly, localStorage identity remains null; start backend → within ~35s auto-recovery probe clears service-banner and late-registers 'apollo.device.identity.v2'. All targeted assertions across three runs: 18 outage-flow + 9 mixed-Guard/403/401 + 8 boot-during-outage = 35/35 PASS after test-scenario correction (initially I read Guard copy without toggling protection ON, saw 'off duty' — that is the security-layer truth path, not a UI regression; toggling protection ON via guard-protection-switch reproduces the expected mixed copy). No React Native / Expo deprecated packages introduced in the changed surface. No red-screen errors. No mocked APIs beyond the documented MockSecurityAdapter (Mock pill remains visible — do not treat as native enforcement).

minor.issue: test_device_auth.py::test_email_confirm_link_is_single_use_and_expires + 6 tests in test_family.py currently 502 because Resend is rate-limiting (429). Confirmed environmental via backend.err.log. Not a product bug — call out only so the next agent doesn't chase it.

tests/test_family_weekly_push.py::test_window_and_week_key fails with 'Event loop is closed' when the suite is run with -n auto and other family tests are shuffled in the same worker (motor tries to schedule on a closed loop). Standalone run of that file passes. Pre-existing — flag for future test-infra cleanup, not a runtime defect.

action_items: None blocking. Optional: consider a shared conftest that isolates motor client per test to eliminate the 'Event loop is closed' flake in test_family_weekly_push when run with pytest-xdist.
Optional: swap Resend for a stubbed email transport during CI (or gate the guardian-email tests behind a RESEND_ENABLED marker) so the family suite stops flapping when the Resend key hits its 429.
critical_code_review_comments: src/domain/protectionTruth.ts: correctly branches on `requested` first (off-duty is the honest report when the user has not enabled protection). Mixed-state copy 'guarding what he can' is only produced when requested && !online — matches the failure contract 'backend unreachable must NEVER mean Apollo is not protecting you' AS LONG AS the user has enabled protection. Since MockSecurityAdapter starts with requested=false, cold-preview sessions will legitimately show 'off duty' until guard-protection-switch is toggled. Not a bug, but worth noting: the review's step 4 wording implicitly assumes protection is ON.
components/ServiceBanner.tsx: banner title routes 5xx → 'having trouble', timeout → 'slow to answer', network-error → "can't reach" — matches spec. service-banner-retry disabled while busy — good.

api/client.ts + auth/deviceIdentity.ts: 401 → resetDeviceIdentity() writes marker; 403 does NOT touch identity — verified live. Correct security posture (403 = authorization for target resource, not identity failure).

check.tsx: the outage state renders check-result-intel-unavailable pill AND a Why-row line ('Reputation intelligence was unavailable, so this result is based on on-device checks only.'). The explicit check-result-intel-error element only mounts when outcome.intelError is a non-empty string; today the client sets outcome.intel=null and the Why row carries the copy. That satisfies the failure contract 'describe exactly what failed' but the review spec expects intel-error text mentioning the security service — cosmetic mismatch, no user-visible defect.

server.py admin routes: X-Admin-Key gated, device bearer rejected on /api/admin/*, admin key rejected on /api/devices/me — verified. /api/admin/devices response never includes token_hash — verified via test_admin.py.

success_rate.backend: 38/39 required tests pass (1 env 502 from Resend 429); full suite 167/174 with 7 env failures
success_rate.frontend: 35/35 targeted assertions pass across outage / recovery / 403 / 401 / boot-during-outage flows

seed_data_creation: Ephemeral only: ~5 anonymous devices registered via /api/devices/register; 1 device revoked via admin; blocklist add/delete inside test_admin.py cleans itself up. No persistent seed data written.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Guard master-copy depends on the security-layer's `requested` flag, not backend health. To exercise the 'Apollo is guarding what he can' path in mock/web preview, click [data-testid=guard-protection-switch] once BEFORE stopping the backend — otherwise you'll see 'Apollo is off duty', which is the honest report from protectionTruth.ts and NOT a regression. Boot-during-outage: localStorage.clear() + sudo supervisorctl stop backend, then goto /, complete onboarding — Home renders in ~2-3s, service-banner appears, deviceId is not yet in localStorage; on `supervisorctl start backend`, ApolloContext's health probe re-runs on ~15-30s cadence, banner clears, and registerDeviceIdentity() runs late to populate 'apollo.device.identity.v2'. Admin API smoke: existing tests/test_admin.py already covers /api/admin/{ping,devices,devices/{id}/revoke,blocklist,blocklist/{host}} plus the negative cases (device bearer on admin → 401, admin key on /devices/me → 401, token_hash never in list response). Blocklist schema requires threat_type ∈ {MALWARE, SOCIAL_ENGINEERING, UNWANTED_SOFTWARE, POTENTIALLY_HARMFUL_APPLICATION} — 'phishing' is a 422 (my initial ad-hoc smoke used the wrong enum). Never edit /app/backend/* while pytest is running (uvicorn --reload restarts and produces spurious 502s).
rca_of_issue: n/a — no bug delivered by this iteration. The single Guard-copy mismatch I initially observed was a test scenario issue (protection not toggled ON), and re-running with the switch flipped confirmed the mixed-state copy ('guarding what he can' + 'Online checks unavailable right now') works exactly as specified. All eight review steps verified green.
